half_life_summaries: SHSMP (Sadat-Habdan mesenchymal stimulating peptide): 90 min (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: HPLC per PEPlife2's Assay field
notes: The single PEPlife2 value of 90 min is verified against the Results text. METHODOLOGICAL CAVEAT: the half-life was not fitted - it is read directly off Figure 3 as the time at which concentration fell to half its initial value ('The peptide reached to the half of its initial concentration ... at 90 min making the plasma half-life of the peptide from the plot is 90 min'). That is a graphical time-to-50% rather than an exponential elimination half-life, and the two coincide only for a single-compartment first-order decay sampled from t=0. No dose, group size, dispersion, strain detail or fitting method is given in the body. The concentrations involved are very low (half of the initial value is 1.16 ng/mL), so the measurement sits near the assay's likely limit of quantitation.

half_life_summaries: Hirulog-1 (bivalirudin): 15 ± 1.3 min (rat plasma) ; Peptide 1 (hirudin mimetic): 13 ± 2.6 min (rat plasma) ; Peptide S2 (stearic-acid-modified peptide 1): 212.2 ± 58.4 min (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: HPLC with MS-MS detection
notes: All three PEPlife2 values are consistent with the body, which states peptide S2's T1/2 = 212.2 ± 58.4 min explicitly and gives 'T1/2 < 16 min' for hirulog-1 and peptide 1, bracketing PEPlife2's 15 ± 1.3 and 13 ± 2.6 min. IDENTICAL SEQUENCE, 16-FOLD DIFFERENT LABEL. PEPlife2 assigns peptide 1 and peptide S2 the SAME sequence string, fPRPGGGGQGDFEPIPEDAYDE, yet records 13 min for one and 212.2 min for the other. The body explains the difference entirely by a modification the string does not encode: S2 'in which the second Gly residue has been replaced with a modified Lys (stearic acid)'. A sequence-to-half-life model sees two contradictory labels for one input, and the 16-fold gap is attributable to a stearoyl group that is invisible in the representation. Note also that the lowercase f in both strings marks D-Phe; the training-set sequence cleaner upper-cases it, so the D-stereochemistry is lost and the residue is read as L-Phe.

half_life_summaries: OT (oxytocin): 0.12 h (rat plasma) ; PF1 (PF-06655075): 8.5 h (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: LC-MS/MS per PEPlife2's Assay field; the body does not describe the bioanalysis
notes: Both PEPlife2 values verified against the Results: oxytocin 0.12 h and PF1 8.5 h after intravenous dosing, a 71-fold difference. Unusually for this cohort the two sequences genuinely DO differ - PF1 is oxytocin with Pro7 to Gly and Leu8 to Lys - so the pair is not a contradictory input. However the modification that actually drives the half-life is not in the sequence: the body attributes it to a PALMITOYL group on that Lys8, 'a lipid tail that confers resistance to clearance' by binding albumin. The two-residue substitution visible in the string is described as a selectivity change (OTR over V1a), not a clearance change. The body reports no dose, strain, sex or group size for the rat PK.

half_life_summaries: ENF (enfuvirtide): 1.5 ± 0.1 h (rat plasma) ; PEG2k-ENF: 16.1 ± 3.8 h (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: HPLC of plasma
notes: Both PEPlife2 values are consistent with the body: 1.5 ± 0.1 h for ENF and 16.1 ± 3.8 h for PEG2k-ENF, a 10.7-fold ratio matching the text's 'over 10-fold longer than that of ENF'. The per-agent figures come from the Figure 4B parameter panel. IDENTICAL SEQUENCE, 10-FOLD DIFFERENT LABEL: PEPlife2 assigns both agents the same enfuvirtide string, so the 2 kDa PEG that causes the entire effect is absent from the representation. Note also that both arms are subcutaneous with no intravenous comparator, and the body describes the conjugate as showing 'a slower but more sustained release profile from the injection site', so part of the difference is slower absorption rather than slower clearance.

half_life_summaries: PEG-HsTX1[R14A]: 37.3 h (rat serum - PEG detected, not the peptide)
bioanalytical_method: Anti-PEG ELISA (PEGylated protein ELISA kit, Enzo Life Sciences); single exponential decay fit
notes: The single PEPlife2 value of 37.3 h is verified against the Results text. TWO CAVEATS. (1) THE ASSAY DETECTS PEG, NOT THE PEPTIDE - quantitation is by an anti-PEG antibody ELISA, so the decay measured is that of the PEG moiety and would not distinguish intact conjugate from PEG still carrying a degraded or cleaved peptide. PEPlife2 records the assay as 'Anti-PEG ELISA', which preserves this, but the half-life is filed against the peptide sequence. (2) tmax is 24 h against a 37.3 h half-life, so this subcutaneous profile is substantially absorption-limited and the terminal value is not a pure clearance half-life. The PEG that causes the effect is not in the stored sequence; the body notes comparable unPEGylated peptide Kv1.3 blockers have rat half-lives 'of less than one hour', so essentially the entire 37-fold extension is attributable to the unencoded moiety. No group size or dispersion on the half-life is given.

half_life_summaries: MS-[Gln28]exenatide microspheres (MeSO2- modulator): 310 hr (rat serum) ; MS-[Gln28]exenatide hydrogel microspheres (-CN modulator): 880 hr (rat serum) ; exenatide (IV): 18 min (rat serum) ; exenatide (SC, absorption phase): 50 min (rat serum) ; [Gln28]exenatide (IV): 17 min (rat serum) ; [Gln28]exenatide (SC, absorption phase): 48 min (rat serum)
bioanalytical_method: LC-MS/MS of serum (assay detail not recoverable from the PDF text)
notes: Read from the publisher PDF, not a PMC deposit. Four of six PEPlife2 values verified directly: 310 hr (Fig. 5A), 880 hr (Fig. 5B), 18 min and 17 min. TWO ARE ABSORPTION HALF-LIVES, NOT ELIMINATION. The body states the SC data follow a flip-flop mechanism with 'rate-determining absorption having a t1/2 of 50 min, followed by an elimination phase with t1/2 of 18 min'. PEPlife2 records those 50 min and 48 min SC values as plain half-lives beside the 18 min and 17 min IV values for the same two peptides, so each peptide appears twice with a 2.8-fold spread that is a phase difference, not a molecular one. PEPlife2 IDs 5998 and 6000 are dropped via CURATED_ABSORPTION, matching how the pipeline already treats every labelled absorption value. Note also the body reports exenatide and [Gln28]exenatide as pharmacokinetically INDISTINGUISHABLE in rodents, so the 18-vs-17 and 50-vs-48 min pairs should not be read as a sequence effect; the second of each pair comes from supplementary Table S3.

half_life_summaries: tag-PK128: t1/2 alpha 0.9+/-0.2 h; t1/2 beta 2.9+/-0.7 h (rat plasma) ; tag-UK18: t1/2 alpha 1.0+/-0.1 h; t1/2 beta 7.4+/-0.2 h (rat plasma) ; UK18 (non-tagged control): t1/2 beta 0.30+/-0.02 h (= 18+/-1 min); t1/2 alpha not determined (rat plasma) ; tag alone: t1/2 alpha 1.5+/-0.4 h; t1/2 beta 12.3+/-0.4 h (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: RP-HPLC (Agilent 1260) with fluorescence detection (ex 445 nm, em 535 nm) on ethanol-precipitated plasma, quantified against standard curves in plasma; two-compartment PK model
notes: All seven PEPlife2 values for this PMID were verified against Table 2 and agree exactly: tag-PK128 0.9/2.9, tag-UK18 1.0/7.4, UK18 0.30 (beta only, alpha n.d.), tag 1.5/12.3 h. This is a two-compartment study, so alpha and beta are separate records and must not be pooled - the spread between them within one animal is up to 8-fold. UK18's 0.30 h agrees with the body's independent statement of 18+/-1 min. The rabbit FXIIa-inhibitor arm (5.2+/-0.4 h tagged vs 13+/-2 min untagged) is a different species and is not part of the rat cohort. Note the authors state the tag binds rat albumin five- to sevenfold more weakly than human albumin, so these rat half-lives understate the expected human values.

half_life_summaries: EXT-Sol (distribution phase): 0.22 ± 0.03 h (rat plasma) ; EXT-SBA-15 (distribution phase): 0.26 ± 0.05 h (rat plasma) ; EXT-Sol (elimination phase): 0.60 ± 0.08 h (rat plasma) ; EXT-SBA-15 (elimination phase): 14.53 ± 0.70 h (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: Exendin-4 ELISA kit (Phoenix Pharmaceuticals EK-070-94); parameters computed in PKSolver 2.0
notes: All four PEPlife2 values verified exactly against Table 1: t1/2(alpha) 0.22 ± 0.03 and 0.26 ± 0.05 h, t1/2(beta) 0.60 ± 0.08 and 14.53 ± 0.70 h. SEQUENCE DEFECT: PEPlife2's string is HGEGTFTSDLSKQMEEEAVRLFIEWLKNGOPSSGAPPPS, which carries an 'O' where exenatide has a glycine (the native sequence is ...IEWLKNGGPSSGAPPPS). O is not one of the 20 standard residues; ESM-2 accepts it as a rare token but carries essentially no pretraining signal for it, so this row and its three siblings are embedded from a slightly corrupted sequence. The body names the drug only as 'Exenatide (mw. 4186.63)' and never prints a sequence, so the error cannot be repaired from the full text. The 24-fold gap between EXT-Sol and EXT-SBA-15 elimination half-lives is a property of the mesoporous silica carrier, not of the peptide: both rows carry the identical sequence, so this pair is a clean illustration of formulation dominating the label.

half_life_summaries: 22A peptide in sHDL (unmodified): 4.588 h (CV 8.58%) (rat serum, 22A peptide by LC-MS (22A plus its 22A(-)Lys metabolite)) ; 22A peptide in sHDL-PEG2k (5%): 4.25 h (CV 17.4%) (rat serum, 22A peptide by LC-MS (22A plus its 22A(-)Lys metabolite)) ; 22A peptide in sHDL-PEG2k (10%): 7.14 h (CV 28.8%) (rat serum, 22A peptide by LC-MS (22A plus its 22A(-)Lys metabolite)) ; 22A peptide in sHDL-PEG5k (5%): 5.05 h (CV 6.34%) (rat serum, 22A peptide by LC-MS (22A plus its 22A(-)Lys metabolite))
bioanalytical_method: LC-MS (Agilent 6520 Q-TOF, negative ion) of methanol-precipitated serum with 5A peptide internal standard; 22A quantified as the sum of 22A and its 22A(-)Lys metabolite
notes: All four PEPlife2 values verified exactly against the T1/2 row of Table 2 (the PEPTIDE table): 4.588, 4.25, 7.14 and 5.05 h. Two cautions. (1) PEPlife2's Test Sample strings misstate the doses - it records 'after 2.5 mg/kg sHDL-PEG2k', 'after 5 mg/kg sHDL-PEG2k' and 'after 2.5 mg/kg sHDL-PEG5k', but the body states every group received 50 mg/kg and the 5/10 figures are PEG MOL PERCENT, not doses (sHDL-PEG2k 5%, sHDL-PEG2k 10%, sHDL-PEG5k 5%); PEPlife2 appears to have halved the percentages and relabelled them mg/kg. The half-life values themselves are correct. (2) Do not confuse these with Table 3, which gives the PHOSPHOLIPID half-lives (4.59, 8.62, 9.96, 12.5 h) for the same animals - the body's headline numbers '8.6 h for sHDL-PEG2k (5%) and 12.5 h for sHDL-PEG5k (5%)' are lipid, not peptide. The paper's own conclusion is that PEGylation did NOT change peptide elimination, so the apparent 4.25-to-7.14 h spread across these four rows is within-group variability (CV up to 28.8%, n = 4), not a PEG effect. The quantified analyte deliberately includes the 22A(-)Lys metabolite.

half_life_summaries: peptide 1b: ~78 min (rat plasma) ; peptide 2d: ~48 min (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: LC-MS/MS per PEPlife2's Assay field; the PDF text does not yield a recoverable bioanalytical description
notes: Read from the publisher PDF; the renderer reported this file as having no separable abstract, so the abstract sits at the top of the body and was identified and avoided. Both PEPlife2 values verified against the Results text: ~78 min for 1b and ~48 min for 2d, both approximate. The body gives no strain, sex or group size; the 5 mg/kg IV dose comes from PEPlife2's own Dose Route and Concentration fields rather than from recoverable body text. SEQUENCE ENCODING: both strings carry non-natural residues written as parenthesised or lowercase codes - (Sar)3 (three sarcosines) and lowercase rr (two D-arginines) in 1b, and hArg (homoarginine) in 2d. The hyphen-delimited codes are now collapsed to a single X each by clean_sequence, but '(Sar)3' encodes a repeat count that no single-character substitution can express, and the lowercase D-residue markers are lost to upper-casing. This paper also reports a ~40 h half-life in rabbit EYES after intravitreal dosing, which is a different species and compartment and is not part of this cohort.

half_life_summaries: 64Cu-DOTA-F56-CM: 6.967 h (rat blood - total 64Cu radioactivity by gamma counting)
bioanalytical_method: Gamma counting of 64Cu radioactivity in whole blood; two-compartment fit in GraphPad Prism 5.01
concentration_time_locator: not separately captioned in the retrieved text
notes: The single PEPlife2 value of 6.967 h is consistent with the described two-compartment analysis of gamma-counted blood radioactivity; the figure itself is not restated in the body text so it could not be checked digit for digit. Caveats. (1) n = 2 RATS per group, so no meaningful precision, and no dispersion is reported. (2) The readout is TOTAL 64Cu RADIOACTIVITY, not intact conjugate - if 64Cu dissociates from the DOTA chelator the label keeps being counted, which for copper-DOTA over a 96 h window is a real possibility. Unlike the total-radioactivity case in 36588717 the paper does not report a parent-drug comparator, so the extent of the discrepancy is unknown. (3) The stored sequence is the bare F56 peptide; the DOTA chelator, the copper and the albumin-binding CM moiety - which the introduction identifies as the half-life-extension mechanism - are all absent from it. The paper notes rat albumin's own half-life is 1.9 days.

half_life_summaries: Liraglutide: 4.2 ± 0.3 h (rat); 3.6 ± 0.2 h (mouse) (rat plasma) ; Analogue 6: 12.9 ± 3.6 h (rat); 10.8 ± 0.8 h (mouse) (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: LC-MS/MS, per PEPlife2's Assay field; the accepted-manuscript PDF text does not describe the bioanalysis in a recoverable form
notes: Read from the publisher PDF (an accepted manuscript, so the text carries interleaved 'ACCEPTED MANUSCRIPT' watermark lines). Both PEPlife2 values verified exactly against the Results text: liraglutide 4.2 ± 0.3 h and analogue 6 12.9 ± 3.6 h in SD rats, both at 50 nmol/kg s.c. Two notes for downstream use. (1) Tmax is 2.0 h for liraglutide and 6.0 h for analogue 6, and both are subcutaneous, so part of the 3-fold half-life difference is slower absorption rather than slower clearance - the paper says so directly ('a slower absorption pattern of 6'). No intravenous arm is reported, so absorption and elimination cannot be separated. (2) PEPlife2's sequence for analogue 6 is a head-to-tail dimer of a 40-residue exendin-4-like sequence, consistent with the paper's dimerization strategy; liraglutide's string is the bare GLP-1 backbone with no palmitoyl protractor, so the lipidation that drives liraglutide's own half-life is absent from its representation.

half_life_summaries: DV1: 8.7 ± 2.4 h (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: HPLC-MS/MS, validated over 10-10000 ng/mL (r > 0.998), with organic additives added to suppress peptide adsorption
concentration_time_locator: Fig. 5, with an inset parameter table
notes: PEPlife2's value of 8.7 ± 2.4 h could NOT be verified numerically: the derived parameters are in a table INSET INTO FIGURE 5, which the PMC BioC deposit does not carry as text. The body confirms the qualitative claim - 'The long half time (t1/2) and the slow reduction after 12 h were observed' - and independently gives Tmax 0.83 ± 0.29 h and Cmax 8592 ± 1056 ng/mL after 10 mg/kg subcutaneous, which PEPlife2 does not record. The value is left uncorrected. STEREOCHEMISTRY LOST: PEPlife2's sequence is written entirely in lowercase, the convention marking an all-D peptide, and the body confirms DV1 is 'a novel D-peptide antagonist of CXCR4'. The training-set sequence cleaner upper-cases it, so an all-D peptide and its all-L enantiomer become the same input - while protease resistance, and therefore much of the half-life, is exactly what the D-configuration buys. The body also attributes the slow terminal phase to tissue redistribution rather than to slow clearance.

half_life_summaries: CNP(1-22) (IV): 1.42 ± 0.45 min (rat plasma, CNP immunoreactivity) ; ASB20123 (IV): 31.3 ± 4.8 min (rat plasma, CNP immunoreactivity) ; CNP(1-22) (SC): 10.0 ± 5.0 min (rat plasma, CNP immunoreactivity) ; ASB20123 (SC): 32.1 ± 8.0 min (rat plasma, CNP immunoreactivity)
bioanalytical_method: Radioimmunoassay for CNP immunoreactivity using antiserum against the 17-membered internal disulfide ring of CNP and [125I]-[Tyr0]-CNP(1-22) tracer
concentration_time_locator: not separately captioned in the retrieved text
notes: All four PEPlife2 values verified against the IV and SC parameter tables: CNP(1-22) 1.42 ± 0.45 min IV and 10.0 ± 5.0 min SC; ASB20123 31.3 ± 4.8 min IV and 32.1 ± 8.0 min SC. PEPlife2 records the last as a bare '32.1', dropping the ±8.0. TWO CORRECTIONS TO PEPlife2 METADATA. (1) The assay is recorded as 'ELISA' but the body says RADIOIMMUNOASSAY, with an antiserum against the CNP disulfide ring and a [125I]-[Tyr0]-CNP(1-22) tracer - an immunoreactivity readout that does not distinguish intact peptide from ring-containing fragments. (2) PEPlife2 records no route, so the IV and SC values for each peptide are indistinguishable in the database; for CNP(1-22) the SC value is 7-fold the IV value, a flip-flop absorption effect rather than a change in clearance. The rats were anaesthetised (pentobarbital, later Inactin) for the whole PK study, which the paper notes but does not control for.

half_life_summaries: FITC-AAR029b: 2.92 ± 0.93 h (rat plasma) ; FITC-AAR029b in Liposome: 8.87 ± 3.17 h (rat plasma) ; FITC-AAR029b (distribution phase): 0.029 ± 0.01 h (rat plasma) ; FITC-AAR029b in Liposome (distribution phase): 0.032 ± 0.005 h (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: Plasma fluorescence (ex 494 nm, em 520 nm) against a FITC-AAR029b calibration curve, with UPLC-Q-TOF MS confirmation that the signal is intact FITC-AAR029b rather than free FITC or fragments
notes: All four PEPlife2 values match the body: elimination 2.92 ± 0.93 h (free) and 8.87 ± 3.17 h (liposomal), distribution 0.029 ± 0.01 and 0.032 ± 0.005 h. Two cautions. (1) n = 2 ANIMALS in total, two per group, run in duplicate - the SD of ±3.17 on the 8.87 h liposomal value spans more than a third of the mean, and no meaningful precision should be read into these numbers. (2) PEPlife2 leaves the Sequence field EMPTY on the two distribution-phase rows while filling it on the two elimination rows, although all four describe the same molecule; the empty rows will be dropped by any sequence-requiring filter, so this study contributes only its two elimination values downstream. Unlike a peptide-targeted carrier, the measured analyte here IS the peptide (fluorescence confirmed as intact FITC-AAR029b by Q-TOF), so the liposomal value is a legitimate peptide half-life. The body reports no dose in mg/kg, only 3 μg fluorescein equivalent.

half_life_summaries: Lysostaphin: 1.5 ± 0.7 h (rat plasma) ; Lst-HDD (helical dimerisation domain fusion): 3.1 ± 0.6 h (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: Sandwich ELISA against lysostaphin antiserum raised in rabbits
notes: Both PEPlife2 values verified exactly: lysostaphin 1.5 ± 0.7 h and Lst-HDD 3.1 ± 0.6 h (p = 0.01). IMPORTANT CONTEXT THAT THE RECORD LOSES: the paper states the elimination is biphasic and that ~95% of BOTH proteins had already been cleared by the first sampling point, 25 minutes after injection - only 2.8 and 1.6 μg/mL remained of a theoretical ~50 μg/mL. These terminal half-lives therefore describe the slow tail of a curve that has already lost almost the whole dose, and are not comparable with a single-phase half-life from a study sampled earlier. The AUC difference is only 2.6-fold, far less than the 10-fold the authors had seen for a covalently dimerised comparator. Note lysostaphin's PEPlife2 sequence carries a C-terminal His6 purification tag, which is part of the dosed material here but is an artefact of expression rather than a designed half-life feature. The body gives no strain, sex or group size.

half_life_summaries: AD-114-PA600: 9.5 h (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: LC-MS/MS per PEPlife2's Assay field
notes: The single PEPlife2 value of 9.5 h is verified exactly against the Results text, for intravenous dosing at 3.5 mg/kg. REPRESENTATION MISMATCH: as with the PASylated thymosin in 33374407, the stored sequence is the ~118-residue AD-114 i-body plus two FLAG tags, while the dosed agent is that i-body fused to a 600-RESIDUE PA polypeptide - the paper's entire half-life-extension strategy, and the reason the same i-body scaffold spans 0.18 h (AD-114-Im7-FH) to 19.24 h (PEG 2x20K) across Table 1. The stored sequence also retains the FLAG purification tags, which are an expression artefact. No strain, sex or group size is given for the rat arm; Table 1's n = 3 applies to the mouse conjugate panel.

half_life_summaries: fasudil in CAR-liposome (intravenous, sham rats): 0.7 ± 0.3 h (rat plasma - FASUDIL concentration, not peptide concentration) ; fasudil in CAR-liposome (intravenous, PAH rats): 1.1 ± 0.3 h (rat plasma - FASUDIL concentration, not peptide concentration) ; fasudil in CAR-liposome (intratracheal, sham rats): 12.9 ± 4.6 h (rat plasma - FASUDIL concentration, not peptide concentration) ; fasudil in CAR-liposome (intratracheal, PAH rats): 16.1 ± 4.1 h (rat plasma - FASUDIL concentration, not peptide concentration)
bioanalytical_method: LC-MS/MS of methanol-deproteinised plasma; non-compartmental analysis in Phoenix WinNonlin
notes: THE MEASURED ANALYTE IS NOT THE PEPTIDE. All four PEPlife2 values verified against the 'fasudil in CAR-liposome' row of Table 4 (IV sham 0.7, IV PAH 1.1, IT sham 12.9, IT PAH 16.1 h), but every one is the plasma half-life of FASUDIL, a small-molecule Rho-kinase inhibitor. The CAR peptide (CARSKNKDC) is a heparan-sulphate-targeting ligand conjugated to the liposome surface; its own concentration is never measured. The paper attributes the extended half-life to liposome accumulation, slow drug release and absorption-controlled elimination, not to any property of the peptide - and the 18-fold spread between the IV and IT values for the identical peptide shows the label is set by the route and formulation, not the sequence. These four records (PEPlife2 IDs 5362-5365) have been excluded via CURATED_NOT_A_HALF_LIFE, because in a sequence-to-half-life training set they would assert that CARSKNKDC has a 16 h half-life.

half_life_summaries: PSG4R (AP25-Fc fusion): 56.270 ± 15.398 h (rat plasma) ; AP25: about 50 minutes (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: Indirect competitive ELISA; parameters computed in DAS 1.0
notes: Both PEPlife2 values verified against the body: PSG4R's elimination half-life is stated as 56.270 ± 15.398 h (PEPlife2 records 56.27), and AP25's as 'about 50 minutes'. The comparison is made explicitly - 'the elimination half-life of PSG4R (56 hours) was much longer than AP25 (around 50 minutes)'. Two caveats. The AP25 value is prior knowledge cited in the Introduction, not measured in this study, and it carries no dose, route, group size or dispersion; its approximate phrasing ('about', 'around') is lost once PEPlife2 stores it as the exact figure 50. And the PSG4R value has an SD of 15.4 h on a 56.3 h mean, with no group size given in the body, so its precision is weak. The 67-fold difference between the two is a real Fc-fusion effect and, unusually for this cohort, the two sequences DO differ - PSG4R carries a helical EAAAK linker and the Fc context that AP25 lacks - so this pair is informative rather than contradictory.

half_life_summaries: PEG2kC34: 2.57 ± 0.71 h (rat plasma (activity-derived)) ; PEG5kC34: 5.11 ± 3.54 h (rat plasma (activity-derived))
bioanalytical_method: INDIRECT: plasma concentration was estimated from an ex vivo anti-HIV-1 inhibition assay, taking the highest dilution causing 50% inhibition, rather than by a chemical assay
concentration_time_locator: PK parameter table; sampling at 0.5-24 h
notes: Both PEPlife2 values verified exactly against the PK parameter table: PEG2kC34 2.57 ± 0.71 h and PEG5kC34 5.11 ± 3.54 h, both subcutaneous at 1.7 μmol/kg, n = 4 (2 male, 2 female). THE ASSAY IS A BIOACTIVITY PROXY, NOT A CONCENTRATION MEASUREMENT. Plasma levels were inferred from the dilution of plasma causing 50% inhibition of HIV-1 infection, so what decays with these half-lives is antiviral ACTIVITY; any inactive metabolite is invisible and any matrix effect on the assay reads as concentration. PEPlife2 records the assay as 'N.A.', losing that distinction. Note the SD on PEG5kC34 is 3.54 h on a 5.11 h mean, so the 2-fold separation between the two conjugates is not well resolved at n = 4. Finally, the two PEPlife2 sequences differ by a single leading cysteine (CWMEW... vs WMEW...), which is almost certainly the PEG attachment residue rather than a real design difference; as stored, the 2-fold half-life difference driven by 2 kDa vs 5 kDa of PEG is represented as the presence or absence of one Cys.

half_life_summaries: RELAX10 (rat, IV): 3.59 days (rat plasma) ; RELAX10 (rat, SC): 3.75 days (rat plasma) ; RELAX10 (mouse, IV): 5.58 days (mouse plasma) ; RELAX10 (mouse, SC): 7.06 days (mouse plasma) ; RELAX10 (mouse, SC dose escalation): 4.59 to 7.06 days (range across three dose levels) (mouse plasma) ; relaxin-2 peptide (serelaxin): 1.1 to 2 minutes in rodents (cited from reference 25, not measured here); 240 minutes in humans (reference 24) (not applicable)
bioanalytical_method: ELISA with anti-Fc monoclonal antibody TM446 (AstraZeneca) as capture and the HRP-conjugated polyclonal from the R&D Systems Relaxin-2 detection kit as detection

notes: All six PEPlife2 values verified exactly against Table 1's rat block: 0.805 (M, 1 mg/kg), 0.248 (F, 1), 0.460 (M, 5), 0.437 (F, 5), 0.341 (M, 75), 0.391 (F, 75) h. Two cautions. half_life_summaries: HM15136: not reported in body (the review states only 'an enhanced 36 hr half-life', with no species, dose or route) (not reported in body)
bioanalytical_method: not reported in body
notes: THIS IS A REVIEW ARTICLE, not a primary study - PubMed publication types are 'Journal Article | Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't | Review', and the paper presents no experiment of its own. PEPlife2 nonetheless records four half-life values against it (66.4 ± 33.0 and 40.9 ± 17.7 h, each duplicated once for the peptide-only and the peptide-plus-Fc sequence, filed as 'Rats serum'). NEITHER VALUE APPEARS IN THE BODY. The only half-life this review states for HM15136 is 'an enhanced 36 hr half-life', given without species, dose, route or citationable detail in the body text; 66.4 and 40.9 h are presumably from the primary HM15136 publication, which this review cites. Per the body-only rule these are recorded as 'not reported in body'. The values have NOT been excluded from the dataset, because they are plausibly real primary measurements; instead a source_is_review flag has been added to build_study_dossier.py and now propagates to in_vivo_half_life.csv, marking these and the 40 other records that come from the cohort's four review articles so they can be weighted or removed deliberately. Note the two PEPlife2 sequences differ (peptide alone vs peptide + IgG4 Fc) while carrying the SAME two half-lives, so this one study contributes two contradictory sequence-to-label mappings.

half_life_summaries: tag-free rhMFG-E8 (beta phase, 2-6 h fit): 1.45 h (rat serum) ; tag-free rhMFG-E8 (beta phase, 2-12 h fit): 2.33 h (rat serum) ; tag-free rhMFG-E8 (alpha phase): 11.55 min (rat serum)
bioanalytical_method: Human MFG-E8 Quantikine ELISA (R&D Systems MFGE80), which does not cross-react with rat MFG-E8; non-compartmental analysis in PKSolver
notes: UNITS ERROR IN PEPlife2, now corrected. The body states the distribution half-life is 11.55 MINUTES; PEPlife2 recorded 11.55 with units 'Hours' (ID 4377), a 60-fold overstatement that also made the distribution phase eight times LONGER than the elimination phase it precedes - an impossibility the record's own numbers should have flagged. Corrected to minutes via UNITS_CORRECTIONS in subset_in_vivo_half_life.py, giving 0.1925 h. That record was in any case already excluded from the training set twice over: PEPlife2 leaves its Sequence field empty, and its phase is distribution rather than a concentration-decay terminal value. The two elimination values are NOT independent measurements: 1.45 h is the beta phase fitted over the 2-6 h window and 2.33 h is the SAME data refitted out to 12 h. The paper's own conclusion is hedged accordingly - 'the beta phase t1/2 of the tag-free rhMFG-E8 is calculated as at least 1.45 h'. Treating them as two observations double-counts one experiment and inflates the apparent spread. n is four independent experiments, not four animals.

half_life_summaries: 1907-B (IV): ~16.8 h (rat plasma) ; semaglutide (IV): ~8 h (rat plasma) ; 1907-B (SC): ~20.5 h (rat plasma) ; semaglutide (SC): ~7.95 h (rat plasma) ; 1907-B (cynomolgus monkey, SC): 84 h (monkey plasma)
bioanalytical_method: In-house LC-MS/MS method; non-compartmental analysis in WinNonlin 6.4
notes: All four PEPlife2 values verified exactly against the Results text: IV 1907-B ~16.8 h and semaglutide ~8 h; SC 1907-B ~20.5 h and semaglutide ~7.95 h. The paper reports them as approximate ('~'), which PEPlife2 preserves. SEQUENCE ENCODING ISSUE, now fixed upstream: both sequences carry an Aib (alpha-aminoisobutyric acid) residue written as a hyphen-delimited three-letter code - 'HsQGTFTSDKSKYLE-Aib-KAAQDFVEWLKAGGPSSGAPPPS' and 'H-Aib-EGTFTSDVSSYLEGQAAKEFIAWLVRGRG'. The training-set sequence cleaner previously upper-cased and stripped punctuation, turning that ONE residue into THREE standard ones (A, I, B); clean_sequence in build_halflife_training_set.py now collapses hyphen-delimited non-natural codes to a single X. Aib appears in 52 records across 10 studies and Sar in 46 across 13, so this affected far more than this paper. Note also the semaglutide sequence here ends ...LVRGRG rather than the canonical ...LVRGRG with the C18 diacid protractor, which PEPlife2 does not encode. PEPlife2 records no route, so the IV and SC pairs are indistinguishable in the database.

half_life_summaries: Aβ11/T80@CSs-TGC: 1.26 ± 0.21 h (rat plasma - TIGECYCLINE concentration, not peptide) ; Free-TGC: 0.77 ± 0.24 h (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: HPLC per PEPlife2's Assay field
notes: EXCLUDED FROM THE TRAINING SET. The measured analyte is TIGECYCLINE, a tetracycline antibiotic - the paper introduces it as 'Tigecycline (TGC), a new-generation tetracycline antibiotic' - loaded into Tween-80-coated chitosan nanoparticles that display an amyloid-beta fragment as a brain-targeting ligand. The paper's own three-arm comparison settles the attribution: the SAME drug has a half-life of 0.77 h free, 0.91 h in plain chitosan nanoparticles and 1.26 h in the targeted ones. PEPlife2 files the 1.26 h value against the sequence CGSNKGAIIGLM, whose own concentration is never measured. PEPlife2 ID 4037 dropped via CURATED_NOT_A_HALF_LIFE.

half_life_summaries: EXT607 (D-VITylated PTH(1-34)): terminal elimination t1/2 ranged from 7 to 15 h across the four rat dose groups (rat plasma) ; EXT607 (cynomolgus monkey): 24 to 32 h (monkey plasma) ; EXT608 (rat steady state): 10 to 14 h (rat plasma)
bioanalytical_method: High Sensitivity Human PTH(1-34) ELISA (Quidel Cat# 60-3900); non-compartmental analysis in Phoenix WinNonlin 6.3
notes: PEPlife2's four values for this PMID (8.43, 15.4, 7.36 and 9.21 h) could NOT be verified individually, because the per-dose-group rat parameters are in Supplementary Table S1, which is not part of the PMC deposit. They are however fully consistent with the body, which states the rat 't1/2 of elimination during the terminal phase ranged from 7 to 15 h' across the four groups (100 μg/kg IV and 30, 100, 300 μg/kg SC) - PEPlife2's minimum and maximum are 7.36 and 15.4 h. The values are left uncorrected. PEPlife2 records no route, so the single IV value and the three SC values are indistinguishable in the database, which matters because SC bioavailability is only 10-13% in the rat. n = 3 per group. The ELISA is a human PTH(1-34) kit, so it measures PTH immunoreactivity rather than the intact D-VITylated conjugate specifically.
